title: Atomic Chat Linux Environment Manifest
description: Schema for the Linux environment manifest: the data about the foundation every managed engine runs on — on which distributions atomic-chat-core may itself install a GPU container runtime — kept apart from engine descriptors. Consumed by atomic-chat-core on Linux only, which caches an accepted manifest by manifest_id and pins an operation to it. One file and one schema per platform: a manifest for another platform never changes the document Linux core reads. A manifest carries data only — no command, no argv, no script: the argv for a recipe is compiled into core, the manifest only names the recipe and where it may run.

schema_version.description: Bump this when the shape of a manifest changes in a backwards-incompatible way.

manifest_id.description: Immutable identifier for this exact published manifest, <platform>-r<N>. Any change, including adding a distribution, MUST be published under a new manifest_id instead of editing this one in place — core caches manifests by this id and pins an operation to the id the user consented to.

platform.description: The platform this manifest describes. Each platform has its own file and schema.

minimum_core_version.description: Lowest atomic-chat-core version that understands this manifest. Core rejects a manifest whose minimum_core_version is above its own version and keeps using the previously accepted one.

recipes.description: Install recipes, as data only: a recipe_id naming argv compiled into core, and the distributions that recipe is qualified to run on. No command, script or argv lives here.

id.description: os-release ID, e.g. ubuntu, debian, fedora.

recipe_id.description: Names argv compiled into core, e.g. linux.install-container-runtime. Never a command or script.

distributions.description: Distributions this recipe has been qualified to run on. Extending support to a new distribution is a new manifest_id here, not a core release and not a new engine descriptor.
